body:
`fn_name` already holds the bin name with hyphens replaced, and the
dispatch loop has been keyed on it all along. The function definition
and the `complete -F` references were the two places still using the
raw bin name, which is what POSIX-mode bash refuses to load.

The command being completed is still the real bin name. Only the
function identifier changes.

subject: fix(mangen): Render the synopsis from override_usage
body:
The SYNOPSIS was always derived from the argument list, which collapses a
command documenting several invocation forms into a single line. A
command that declared them through `Command::override_usage` ended up
with a manual page whose synopsis contradicted the rest of the text: the
`ln` utility of uutils/coreutils, for instance, listed one form while its
after-help referred to the 1st through 4th forms.

Render the synopsis from `Command::override_usage` when it is set, one
line per form, and keep deriving it from the arguments otherwise.

Fixes uutils/coreutils#12366 and #6466

refactor(builder): Rename internal blacklist field to conflicts
body:
`Arg::blacklist` holds the ids an argument conflicts with. `conflicts`
names that directly, matches the public `conflicts_with` API it backs,
and sits alongside the existing `overrides`, `groups`, and `requires`
fields.

The field is `pub(crate)`, so this is not a public API change. The only
externally visible effect is the `Arg` `Debug` output, where the field
prints as `conflicts` instead of `blacklist`.

subject: fix(help): Bracket values past the minimum
body:
An option declared with a value-count range, like `num_args(1..=2)` with
two value names, rendered as

    --example <FOO> <BAR>

while the parser accepts `--example FOO`, so the help contradicted what
the parser would take. Render the value names past the minimum as
optional instead

    --example <FOO> [BAR]

An option whose value is optional as a whole is bracketed by
`stylize_arg_suffix`, so its names stay unbracketed to avoid `[[name]]`.

Fixes #4847

subject: fix(complete): Don't glob-expand bash positionals
body:
For a positional arg with no possible_values, the bash generator wrote
its Display placeholder (e.g. `[ARG]`) as a literal completion word.
Bash then glob-expands the unquoted brackets in
`COMPREPLY=($(compgen -W "${opts}" -- "${cur}"))`, matching
filenames in the cwd instead of offering the placeholder as text.

Positionals without possible values now contribute no completion word
and fall through to the existing -o default file-completion fallback,
matching how the zsh generator already behaves for the same case.

Fixes #6407

subject: fix(complete): Two-pass quote fish env-completer
body:
Fish parses `--arguments` once at the outer level, then again when
`(...)` is evaluated. Top-level single-quote is enough for the bin
arg; the completer path inside `(...)` needs the second-pass escape
or backslashes and $ get unquoted before the completer runs.

Adds `fish_quote` (top-level) and `fish_quote_for_eval`
(second-pass: \\, \$, \') and routes the registration through them.

subject: fix(complete): Keep zsh candidate order
feat(complete): Index-aware ValueCompleter
body:
Add `ValueCompleter::complete_at(arg_index, current)` and a
matching `ArgValueCompleter::complete_at` shim. The default
trait impl delegates to `complete`, so existing implementors are
unaffected. The dynamic engine now threads each value's position
within an argument's `num_args` range into the completer, so a
multi-value argument can return different candidates per slot
(for example, a remote name first and a branch name second for
`--set-upstream <REMOTE> <BRANCH>`).

`arg_index` counts shell arguments and is unaffected by
`value_delimiter`.

Closes #6284

subject: fix(derive): Track Cargo env vars for incremental rebuilds
body:
clap_derive reads CARGO_PKG_NAME, CARGO_PKG_AUTHORS, CARGO_PKG_VERSION,
and CARGO_PKG_DESCRIPTION via std::env::var() during macro expansion.
Since proc_macro::tracked_env::var is still unstable, rustc never learns
about these reads, so Cargo does not rebuild when the values change in
Cargo.toml.

Fix by injecting a no-op env! call alongside each baked-in value in the
generated code.  rustc tracks these at compile time and reports them to
Cargo, which then triggers a rebuild on change.

The tracking is emitted only when the env var was actually accessed and
returned a non-empty value (CARGO_PKG_NAME) or is embedded directly in
the method argument block (CARGO_PKG_AUTHORS, CARGO_PKG_VERSION,
CARGO_PKG_DESCRIPTION via Method::from_env).

Fixes #6333

Made-with: Cursor

subject: fix(complete): Do not suggest options after "--"

fix: Allow optional value arguments for Zsh shell completion
body:
When dealing with an argument that can optionally take a value, the
shell completion file generated for Zsh doesn't actually specify any
value being allowed (because that string gets repeated 0 times when
generating the completion script, which results in not actually being
written to the completion script). This results in completion being
partially broken if that option gets specified with a value.

Fix this by having a special case for 0 arguments, where a `:` gets
prepended to the value completion. This tells zsh that specifying a
value is optional here.

Signed-off-by: Saikrishna Arcot <saiarcot895@gmail.com>

fix(complete): Trailing space after zsh directory completions
body:
zsh dynamic completions would add a trailing space after all
completions, including directories. This prevented natural path
completion. Users had to delete the trailing space before continuing to
type or tab-complete within the directory.

The fix is for the dynamic completion script to separate completions
into directories and non-directories, and providing the directory
completions to zsh with a different _describe invocation.

For directories:
1. Strip the trailing slash from the completion value
2. Let zsh add it back as a suffix using `_describe -S '/'`
3. Also provide `-r '/'` to make the slash auto-removable when typing '/'

This makes dynamic path completions reasonably emulate zsh-native file
completions.

subject: fix(complete): Follow symlinks in path completion
body:
On Unix, `DirEntry::metadata()` is equivalent to `symlink_metadata()`,
which returns metadata about the symlink itself rather than the target.
This caused symlinks to directories to be incorrectly classified as
non-directories, preventing them from appearing in path completions.

Use `Path::is_dir()` instead, which follows symlinks to check if the
target is a directory.

Fixes #6201

subject: fix(clap_mangen): Take into consideration display_order
body:
In #3362 we have an issue where when we configure an arg via
.display_order(int), and then generate a manpage,
the synposis and options will render the order the args were
provided to the App rather than the order they were configured

e.g

Command::new(name)
arg(Arg::new("few").short('b').display_order(2))
arg(Arg::new("bar").short('a').display_order(1))

will show

...
SYNOPSIS
    <name> [-b] [-a] ...

...
OPTIONS
    -b
    -a

instead of

...
SYNOPSIS
    <name> [-a] [-b] ...

...
OPTIONS
    -a
    -b

and so on. This fix adds sorting in the synopsis and
options functions responsible for generating the
corresponding synopsis and options sections of the manpage.

Co-authored-by: ericgumba <ericgumba@gmail.com>
